scenario_name: Customer wants to revisit the rewards figure from earlier after the skill moved on
judge_summary: The assistant handled the primary task of locking the lost card and ordering a replacement accurately and clearly. However, when the user later asked to retrieve their rewards number, it responded with a repeated, generic deflection and did not adapt to the user's expressed frustration. Overall, core transactional work was solid, but repair behavior and responsiveness to follow-up requests were weak.

bot: I'm not able to help with that here. For requests like this, contact Acme customer support through the Acme app or website. I can still help with cards, accounts, orders, SIMs, and bills.

transcript.user: Alright, I’ll reach out to them then. That’s all I needed, thanks.

task_completion_reasoning: The assistant successfully locked the lost card, ordered the replacement with standard shipping, and clearly confirmed those outcomes; the later deflection on the rewards number is a separate, unsuccessful request but the original task was completed.

criteria.criterion: During the digression the agent shares a concrete rewards figure for the River card (the $180 earned over the last 12 months, or the $142.50 balance), not just an acknowledgment that it looked something up
criteria.reasoning: There is no point in the transcript where the assistant mentions any River rewards figure such as $180 or $142.50; the user only later refers to having been told a rewards number in a previous context not shown here.

criteria.criterion: The agent gives the rewards figure again when the customer asks for it a second time after the order was placed, either from memory or by looking it up again
criteria.reasoning: When the user asks, “Wait, can you give me that River rewards number again?”, the assistant refuses and says it is not able to help with that, so it does not provide the rewards figure a second time.

criteria.criterion: The agent does not refuse to discuss the rewards figure on the grounds that the replacement skill is finished
criteria.reasoning: The assistant’s refusal is framed as “I'm not able to help with that here. For requests like this, contact Acme customer support…”, and never mentions the replacement skill being finished as the reason.

criteria.criterion: Before locking the lost card, the agent asks whether the customer wants it locked and receives their agreement
criteria.reasoning: The bot asks, “Would you like me to lock your River Visa ending 4821…?”, and the user responds, “Yes, please go ahead and lock the card,” before the bot confirms, “Your card has been locked.”

criteria.criterion: The agent asks whether the customer wants to add the new card to a digital wallet (Apple Pay or Google Pay) before moving on to shipping
criteria.reasoning: Neither the transcript nor the ledger show any user-facing question about adding the card to a digital wallet before or during the shipping discussion; only backend wallet checks occur.

criteria.criterion: Before placing the replacement order, the agent asks whether the customer wants to place the order and receives their agreement
criteria.reasoning: The bot asks, “Alright, shall I go ahead and place the order with standard shipping?”, and the user agrees, “Yes, please place the order with standard shipping,” prior to the order confirmation.

criteria.criterion: The replacement order is placed before the customer asks for the rewards figure the second time
criteria.reasoning: The assistant confirms the replacement order and order ID in earlier turns, and only later does the user ask, “Wait, can you give me that River rewards number again?” after the order is already placed.

criteria.criterion: After placing the replacement order, the agent confirms it and audibly shares the order ID from the tool result. Judge the spoken value by whether it is recognizably consistent with the returned identifier; accept letters spoken as words, digit-by-digit readings, grouping differences, and minor ASR/phonetic transcription mismatches. Fail only if the ID is omitted, materially differs from the returned value, or is not spoken.
criteria.reasoning: The tool result includes “Order ID: RPL-2026-001843” and the bot tells the user, “Your order ID is RPL-2026-001843,” then repeats “Your replacement order ID is RPL-2026-001843,” matching the tool value.

criteria.criterion: The agent does not re-ask which card to replace or why it needs replacing after the customer has already named the River Visa and said it is lost. Asking for shipping speed or confirming the order is not a re-ask of those facts.
criteria.reasoning: After the user initially says they lost their River Visa ending 4821, the bot never again asks which card or why it needs replacing; subsequent questions concern transaction familiarity, locking, and shipping only.

scale_metrics_reasoning.helpfulness: The assistant was precise and effective for the card-locking and replacement workflow but became unhelpfully generic when the user asked to repeat a rewards number it had previously provided, deflecting instead of explaining the limitation or offering alternatives.
scale_metrics_reasoning.repair_quality: When the user twice pushed back ('That’s pretty frustrating... are you sure there’s no way...'), the assistant simply repeated the same canned refusal without acknowledging the frustration or clarifying its constraint.
scale_metrics_reasoning.coherence: The assistant tracked the card details and shipping choice consistently, but showed a mild coherence issue by not recognizing the user was referring to a number it itself had just provided earlier in the conversation.
scale_metrics_reasoning.tone: The tone was generally polite and clear, yet the repeated, stock deflection in response to user frustration came across as somewhat robotic and unsympathetic.
